bridge_togetsukyo.note: OSM centerline ends at the abutments; the 155 m figure is the published length. Width sources disagree (11 m vs 12.2 m); OSM sidewalk centerlines are ~8.7 m apart.

facts._note: Each fact has v (value), src (URLs) and, where it matters, how sure it is. 'snippet' means the source page could not be loaded directly and the value comes from its search-result excerpt.

bamboo_species.v: Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis); OSM also tags the grove genus=Phyllostachys, species=Phyllostachys edulis

bamboo_height.v: Species can reach ~20-28 m; grove stalks are usually described as roughly 10-20 m. For the game: 15-20 m culms, tops leaning in over the path into a tunnel.
bamboo_height.lean: Stalks rise straight then lean inward toward the path near the top (described as a bamboo tunnel).
bamboo_height.conf: species max 28 m (Wikipedia, read); grove-specific 10-15 m is from a travel guide (search excerpt), not a survey

bamboo_color.v: Bright green canes, becoming dull yellow(-green) with age; dense green canopy overhead.

bamboo_culm_diameter.conf: 22 cm max read on Wikipedia; 8-18 cm range from a search excerpt

bamboo_spacing.derived: from moso stand densities of ~4,000-10,000 culms/ha (spacing = 1/sqrt(density)); e.g. 6,900 and 9,700 culms/ha in a Japanese moso stand, ~3,900/ha in managed Kagoshima stands
bamboo_spacing.conf: general moso data, not measured at Arashiyama (no Arashiyama-specific source found)

bamboo_count.v: tens of thousands of stalks (数万本) around the path

path_length.v: about 400 m for the classic Nonomiya Shrine - Tenryu-ji north gate - Okochi Sanso path; about 500 m including the connecting sections. OSM 竹林の道 ways measure the value in bamboo_path.len_m.

path_width.v: about 4-5 m between the fences (single-lane paved lane, concrete/asphalt; open to vehicles per OSM note)
path_width.conf: ESTIMATE: no published width found; OSM has no width tag (it is tagged a one-lane public road)

fences.v: Fences of bundled dried bamboo branches (brushwood) line both sides of the path. Japanese sources call them hogaki (穂垣, bamboo-branch fences), a brushwood fence of the shiba-gaki (柴垣) family; Kyoto Prefecture thins the Sagano groves partly to supply the bamboo branches for repairing them. A separate rickshaw lane runs without fences.
fences.height: roughly 1.5-2 m (estimate; not found in a source)
fences.conf: hogaki naming from the Japanese government page and the Kyoto Prefecture PDF (both search excerpts; the pages refused/failed direct fetch); shibagaki = 'a very old type of brushwood fencing' (JAANUS, read) is the general family term, not the name these sources use

togetsukyo_length.alt: Japanese Wikipedia also gives 158 m for the 1934 structure in its history section; OSM centerline measures ~153 m

togetsukyo_width.alt: 11 m per kyoto-en.mytabi.net; 12.2 m (幅員) per Japanese Wikipedia; OSM sidewalk centerlines are ~8.7 m apart, consistent with ~11 m overall

togetsukyo_structure.v: Completed 1934. Columns and beams are reinforced concrete (steel-reinforced concrete girder bridge); only the parapets/railings are wooden (hinoki cypress, square-lattice), which is why it looks like a wooden bridge. First bridge at the site ~836.

river_name.v: Katsura River (桂川) downstream of Togetsukyo; upstream of the bridge it is the Oi (大堰川), and the Kameoka - Hozu gorge stretch of the Oi is called the Hozu (保津川). OSM has an information board named 大堰川 near the bridge.

crowds.v: Go early: before about 8:00 (6-8 a.m. is quietest, soft light), or after ~17:00. Weekdays are quieter; late morning-afternoon is the peak; worst around early April (cherry) and the second half of November (autumn leaves). The path is free and open 24 h but not lit at night (except the December Hanatouro light-up).
crowds.conf: 7-8 a.m. weekday advice read on solosophie; 6-8 a.m./after 17:00 from japancheapo (search excerpt); season peaks from japan-guide (read)

tenryuji.v: Rinzai Zen head temple (OSM start_date 1345); part of the UNESCO World Heritage site 'Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto' (inscribed 1994; OSM ref:whc 688-012). Hours 8:30-17:00 (last entry 16:50). Garden ¥500 (high school and up), ¥300 elementary/middle school, preschool free; buildings +¥300; Hatto (Cloud Dragon painting) separate ¥500, weekends/holidays and special spring/autumn periods. Sogenchi garden by Muso Soseki is a Special Place of Scenic Beauty.
tenryuji.conf: hours/fees/UNESCO statement read on the official site (2026 page); inscription year 1994 and component ref from OSM whc tags; 'Special Place of Scenic Beauty' from memory, unverified

okochi_sanso.v: Former villa of actor Okochi Denjiro (1896-1962) at the west end of the grove; 9:00-17:00; ¥1,000 incl. matcha and a sweet.

monkey_park.v: Monkey Park Iwatayama: entrance/ticket booth on the south bank just upstream of Togetsukyo; the free-roaming monkey area is up a steep trail, about a 10-minute hike per japan-guide (other guides say ~20 min).

sagano_romantic_train.v: Sagano Scenic Railway (Sagano Torokko / Romantic Train): sightseeing train on the old San'in line along the Hozu gorge, Torokko Saga - Torokko Arashiyama - Hozukyo - Torokko Kameoka, about 7 km (7.3 km) in ~25 min; one car (No. 5 'Rich') has no windows; seats are reserved. Its tracks run next to the JR Sagano line; Torokko Saga/Arashiyama stations are in this pack (OSM 嵯峨野観光鉄道).

hozugawa_boats.v: Hozugawa river boat ride (Hozugawa Kudari): traditional flat-bottomed boats, piloted by boatmen with oars and bamboo poles, run down the Hozu gorge from Kameoka to Arashiyama (~16 km) in about 2 hours, arriving a few hundred metres upstream of Togetsukyo (OSM ferry stop 保津川下り下船場). Fares differ by source; check the official site.
hozugawa_boats.conf: boat type, 2 h and landing point read on japan-guide; 16 km from search excerpts; hozugawakudari.jp is the operator's site (from OSM website tag), not loaded
